paper.title_en: The production of lepton pairs in heavy-ion collisions at SPS and RHIC energies
paper.abstract_en: We perform a quantitative study of dilepton production and elliptic flow in In+In collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}=17.3$ GeV and isobar collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}=200$ GeV, concentrating on the low and intermediate invariant mass regions. The medium evolution is simulated event-by-event with the multistage iEBE-MUSIC framework, and the electromagnetic emission combines for the first time quark-gluon plasma (QGP) emission calculated at next-to-leading order (NLO) in the strong coupling with in-medium radiation calculated with hadronic many-body theory. Freeze-out and surviving primordial $ρ$ decays are also included. The calculations are compared with the high-precision dimuon spectra measured by the NA60 Collaboration, and with STAR preliminary measurements of dielectron spectra and elliptic flow. We obtain effective temperatures extracted from the transverse-mass spectra, and we calculate the elliptic flow of the different dilepton sources. Our results suggest that dilepton measurements in the low-mass and high $p_T$ region can provide insight into higher-order corrections to the QGP emission rate.
